claim: PTEN is a tumor suppressor that dephosphorylates the lipid second messenger phosphatidyl inositol 3,4,5-triphosphate (PIP3).
source: PTEN (phosphatase and tensin homolog deleted on chromosome 10) suppresses cell proliferation, migration and survival by dephosphorylating the lipid second messenger phosphatidyl inositol 3,4,5-triphosphate (PIP3), thereby opposing phosphatidyl inositol-3 kinase (PI3K) signaling and preventing AKT protein kinase activation (Maehama and Dixon, 1998; Myers et al., 1998; Sun et al., 1999; Iijima and Devreotes, 2002).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations to prior research establishing PTEN's function

claim: PTEN opposes phosphatidyl inositol-3 kinase (PI3K) signaling and prevents AKT protein kinase activation.
source: PTEN (phosphatase and tensin homolog deleted on chromosome 10) suppresses cell proliferation, migration and survival by dephosphorylating the lipid second messenger phosphatidyl inositol 3,4,5-triphosphate (PIP3), thereby opposing phosphatidyl inositol-3 kinase (PI3K) signaling and preventing AKT protein kinase activation (Maehama and Dixon, 1998; Myers et al., 1998; Sun et al., 1999; Iijima and Devreotes, 2002).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations to prior research

claim: PTEN is one of the most frequently mutated genes in cancer.
